description:
The team consists of Yi-Lin, an AI product designer with over 8 years of experience in B2C SaaS product design and psychology/HCI (human-computer interaction) background, exploring human-centered design in space field.

With a non-engineering background, they used AI as a development partner while taking ownership of product decisions, UX/UI design, implementation, and quality assurance.
summary: ASTRAVIA goes beyond health monitoring, helping astronauts know what to do next when immediate medical support from Earth is unavailable. By turning personal health data and spaceflight risks into actionable guidance, it helps crews assess their condition and readiness for critical missions. ASTRAVIA supports independent health decisions, reduces preventable risks, and protects both crew well-being and mission safety.
details:
Millions of kilometers from Earth, astronauts cannot always rely on immediate medical support. During long-duration space missions, even subtle health changes can affect their well-being and ability to perform critical tasks. How can astronauts make informed health decisions when Earth cannot respond?

Overview

ASTRAVIA is a health copilot that helps astronauts move from uncertainty to informed action.
By combining wearable data and self-assessments, it visualizes changes from personal health baselines through an interactive body map. Guided care helps astronauts understand symptoms and take appropriate action, while mission readiness checks evaluate how health and environmental risks may affect upcoming tasks.
Imagine an astronaut experiencing a headache before a spacewalk. ASTRAVIA helps identify potential contributing factors, guides the astronaut through the next steps, and flags the mission for reassessment when necessary.

What makes ASTRAVIA different is its mission-aware approach

Feeling healthy doesn't always mean being ready for a task. By connecting personal health, environmental conditions, and mission requirements, ASTRAVIA goes beyond monitoring to support safer decisions.
NASA Human Research Program findings informed which health indicators to monitor and how spaceflight hazards might affect them. Rather than treating every deviation as a diagnosis, ASTRAVIA emphasizes personal baselines, possible contributing factors, and clear boundaries for seeking medical support.

Design and development

ASTRAVIA was independently researched, designed, and developed by a product designer using Vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and Tailwind CSS, with Claude Code assisting in coding, writing, and product design iteration.

Github repo: https://github.com/yi-linchuang/astravia
